newsletter.subject: Vellmont council passes budget
newsletter.text:
The Vellmont city council approved a $2.1 billion budget for next year on Tuesday, by a vote of 9 to 2.

The budget adds 60 police officers and 45 firefighters, puts $80 million toward road repairs, and raises the property tax rate by 1.5%. Mayor Odette Ferrand called it "the budget that finally fixes the potholes".

referenceSummary: The Vellmont city council approved a $2.1 billion budget for next year on Tuesday, by a vote of 9 to 2. It adds 60 police officers and 45 firefighters, puts $80 million toward road repairs and raises the property tax rate by 1.5%, which Mayor Odette Ferrand said would finally fix the potholes. Council member Ruth Ambler, who voted no, said the tax increase would hurt renters. A vote on a new library branch was postponed until January, and public comment on the capital plan is open until December 12.
